          London City Lionesses vs Manchester City Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 30, 2026
          
                      Louise Beltrame-Bawden / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Sunday's WSL showdown with our London City Lionesses vs Manchester City preview. Can London City prove they are genuine contenders for the WSL crown, or will City underline why they remain the team to beat?

Since Michelle Kang acquired London City Lionesses in December 2023, the club's transformation has been nothing short of remarkable, and this fixture could provide the clearest indication yet of their title credentials.
Their Spanish superstar Alexia Putellas has been back in the headlines this week after claiming her third Ballon d'Or, reflecting the increasingly international identity of this London City side.
Seven of the Lionesses' starting XI against Liverpool last weekend were Spanish, with Putellas and Daniela Arques joining an entirely Spanish back five, including goalkeeper Elene Lete.

It marked the first time in WSL history that a team had named seven players from the same non-British nation in their starting lineup. However, that recruitment strategy has also meant limited opportunities for English players.
Freya Godfrey, with five, is the only England international to have started more than twice in the league for Eder Maestre’s side this season.
Yet, whatever the makeup of their squad, the results suggest Kang's investment is beginning to pay off.
London City have won their last five WSL home matches, a run bettered only by City's remarkable sequence of 16 such victories.
Another win on Sunday would see the Lionesses become the first team outside the traditional ‘big four' to win six successive WSL home games.
On the other hand, the reigning champions remain unbeaten after seven league matches (W6 D1) and could avoid defeat in their opening eight games of a WSL campaign for the first time since 2018-19.
But, there is evidence that Maestre’s team are learning how to match the division’s elite.
Having lost each of their first seven league encounters against those teams, London City have collected four points from their last two.
Now comes arguably their biggest test yet against the reigning champions.
One of the keys to London City's success has been their fast starts. They've already scored eight goals inside the opening 30 minutes of WSL games this season, the most of any side.
Such an approach means Maestre’s side have spent a league-high 68% of their total playing time in a winning position.

And Man City will need to pay particular attention to the Lioness’s threat down the left; a league-high 44% of London City’s attacking touches have come down that flank, while in each of their last three league matches, the player starting on the left wing has found the net.

That threat down the left could prove particularly significant on Sunday, especially given City's recent defensive uncertainty in that position, having changed their starting right-back in each of their last five WSL matches.
But while there may be questions about City's defensive consistency in wide areas, there are few doubts about their attacking fluency.

Jeglertz’s sidce remain one of the WSL's most accomplished possession-based teams, recording the third-highest average possession (61%) and the joint-most open-play sequences of 10 or more passes (116) this season.
Their sequences also average more passes (4.3) and last longer (12.2 seconds) than those of any other side, highlighting their ability to control possession and dictate the tempo of matches.
